title: Women Have Been Such An Important Part of the Cannabis Reform Movement, But Their Pain Problems Have Not Been Adequately Addressed

content_html_sanitized:
The US and the UK have very different medical systems, but -unfortunately- they have some things in common. In both countries, women’s pain problems are under addressed, and in both countries the medical establishment has failed their patients, especially regarding medical cannabis.

See The UK Has Some of the Highest Drug Overdose Death Rates in Europe But The New York Times Does A Major Story On “Cali Weed” Smuggled Into The UK and Misses the Real Story

And

Why Is the UK Still Failing Children Who Need Medical Cannabis?

And from 1998

Mademoiselle Magazine Features Long Article On The Importance of Medical Marijuana For Women

(How time flies, when you’re not in pain or in prison)

 

But even now, See

Study Finds Women Less Likely to be Prescribed Pain Medications

 

Last Saturday, The Independent, UK’s center left broadsheet, carried an interesting article about the difficulties that women have getting proper treatment for their pain problems. However, they have even more difficulty getting access to medical cannabis under their National Health Service.

See

Over-the-counter pain relief failed me – but I started to embrace life again when I turned to medical cannabis’

 

In addition to the under treatment of the pain suffered by both men and women, women have problems getting treatment for pain associated with their menstrual problems.

See

Can Weed Help with Period Cramps?

 

From Harvard Health Are women turning to cannabis for menopause symptom relief?

“Now, one survey suggests nearly 80% of midlife women use cannabis to ease certain symptoms, such as mood issues and trouble sleeping.”

See

The New York Post Can’t Figure Out Why Pregnant Women Use Cannabis. Perhaps Because They Are Not Getting Adequate Medical Care?

 

On The Titanic it was “Women and Children First.” On the slowly sinking Cannabis Prohibition, it is “Women and Children Last.”
